sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Colma.
sentences.zh: 科尔马。

sentences.en: About 10 miles south of San Francisco, out toward the airport, there's a town called Colma.
sentences.zh: 在旧金山以南大约10英里处，朝向机场的方向，有一个名叫科尔马的小镇。

sentences.en: I have never been to Colma before, but it's cool you can take the train right here.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未去过科尔马，但你能坐火车直接到这里，这真的很酷。

sentences.en: That's producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人埃弗里·特拉夫曼。

sentences.en: Oh, all right.
sentences.zh: 噢，好的。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Right beyond the train station are already these big, rolling, green hills, peppered with tombstones.
sentences.zh: 火车站外面不远处就是这些巨大的、起伏的绿色山丘，上面点缀着墓碑。

sentences.en: 73% of the land in Colma is covered with graveyards.
sentences.zh: 科尔马73%的土地都被墓地覆盖。

sentences.en: Oh, and they're just rows and rows of big gravestones that look like little houses.
sentences.zh: 噢，而且全都是一排排的大墓碑，看起来像一座座小房子。

sentences.en: There are 17 full-size cemeteries together in one town.
sentences.zh: 这个小镇上总共有17座标准规模的公墓。

sentences.en: 18, if you include the Pet Cemetery.
sentences.zh: 算上宠物公墓的话就是18座。

sentences.en: This is huge.
sentences.zh: 这太宏大了。

sentences.en: It is a city of the dead, what's known as a necropolis.
sentences.zh: 这是一座死者之城，也就是所谓的死者之都。

sentences.en: We claim to be the only necropolis in the United States, anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们自称是美国唯一的死者之都。

sentences.en: The only city that is primarily dedicated to cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 唯一一座主要由公墓构成的城市。

sentences.en: This is Maureen O'Connor, president of the Colma Historical Association.
sentences.zh: 这是莫琳·奥康纳，科尔马历史协会的主席。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that there are a lot of cities that don't have cemeteries within their boundaries, but nothing of the concentration that we have here.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说没有许多城市在其边界内没有公墓，但没有哪个城市能达到我们这里的集中程度。

sentences.en: And Colma truly looks like a sprawling city, a landscape of mausoleums and monuments and towers and tombstones that glint in the sun for as far as the eye can see.
sentences.zh: 科尔马看起来确实像一座无边无际的城市，这是一片由陵墓、纪念碑、塔楼和墓碑组成的景观，在阳光下闪闪发光，一望无际。

sentences.en: But it is eerily quiet.
sentences.zh: 但这里静得可怕。

sentences.en: Here, the dead outnumber the living 1,000 to 1.
sentences.zh: 在这里，死者与生者的比例是1000比1。

sentences.en: We have 1,600 living citizens, and we have about 1.5 million residents who live underground or in mausoleuMs.
sentences.zh: 我们有1600名活着的市民，大约有150万名居民住在地下或陵墓里。

sentences.en: Maureen talks about her dead neighbors and her living neighbors with the same vocabulary, like when she referred to John Daly, the long-deceased dairy magnate.
sentences.zh: 莫琳用完全相同的词汇来谈论她死去的邻居和活着的邻居，比如她提到已故多年的乳业大亨约翰·戴利时。

sentences.en: John Daly, for whom Daly City is named, one of our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 约翰·戴利，戴利城就是因他而得名，他是我们的邻居之一。

sentences.en: She has a lot of famous neighbors, like Joe DiMaggio and Levi Strauss of Levi Jeans, and Tina Turner's dog is in the pet cemetery.
sentences.zh: 她有很多著名的邻居，比如乔·迪马乔和李维斯牛仔裤的创始人李维·施特劳斯，蒂娜·特纳的狗也安葬在宠物公墓里。

sentences.en: They're all around, and Maureen's house is literally sandwiched between two different cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 他们无处不在，莫琳的房子实际上就夹在两个不同的公墓之间。

sentences.en: I live across from the Italian cemetery, in the front of my house, and then the back of my backyard borders with the Japanese cemetery.
sentences.zh: 我住在意大利公墓对面，就在我家前面，然后我后院的后面与日本公墓相邻。

sentences.en: And then I have two human neighbors on east and weSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我在东西两侧有两个活着的邻居。

sentences.en: The official town motto of Colma is, it's great to be alive in Colma.
sentences.zh: 科尔马官方的镇训是，在科尔马活着真好。

sentences.en: It's great to be alive in Colma.
sentences.zh: 在科尔马活着真好。

sentences.en: Colma had many lives before it became the modern necropolis, before it was even called Colma.
sentences.zh: 在成为现代死者之都之前，甚至在被称为科尔马之前，这座小镇经历过许多次转变。

sentences.en: In the 1800s, it was rich farmland, since it caught all the moisture off the bay, and most of the vegetables for San Francisco were grown there.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，这里是肥沃的农田，因为它捕捉了海湾所有的湿气，旧金山大部分的蔬菜都是在那里种植的。

sentences.en: At another point, it was known mostly for hog farming, and at another point, it was known for cultivating flowers.
sentences.zh: 在另一个时期，这里主要以养猪业闻名，而在另一个时期，则以培育花卉闻名。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, a few miles north, in San Francisco proper, people were pouring in because of the gold rush.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在几英里以北的旧金山本部，由于淘金热，人们如潮水般涌入。

sentences.en: The population was booming, and so was the death rate.
sentences.zh: 人口激增，死亡率也随之上升。

sentences.en: Well, certainly there was an enormous amount of death at that time, and just because there were no antibiotics,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时确实有大量的人死亡，仅仅是因为没有抗生素，

sentences.en: people died of stuff that you wouldn't even think of dying of now.
sentences.zh: 人们会死于现在你连想都不会想到会因此丧命的东西。

sentences.en: San Francisco's cemeteries started to fill up.
sentences.zh: 旧金山的公墓开始装不下了。

sentences.en: And starting in 1887, religious groups and organizations began, one by one, to buy plots of land south of the city
sentences.zh: 从1887年开始，宗教团体和组织开始一个接一个地在城市南部买下土地，

sentences.en: to create new burial grounds, which eventually covered over two square miles.
sentences.zh: 来建立新的墓地，最终这些墓地覆盖了超过两平方英里的面积。

sentences.en: In 1924, the cemeteries got together, and they decided to incorporate.
sentences.zh: 1924年，各大公墓联合起来，决定组建公司。

sentences.en: Those 2.2 square miles officially became a town, a cemetery town, called Lawndale,
sentences.zh: 这2.2平方英里的土地正式变成了一个镇，一个墓地小镇，名叫朗戴尔，

sentences.en: which in 1941 would be renamed Colma.
sentences.zh: 它在1941年更名为科尔马。

sentences.en: And all of this was happening in the context of a much bigger change in American burial practices.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都发生在美国葬礼习俗发生巨大变化的背景下。

sentences.en: For a long time, the dead used to be buried in little squares or churchyards on dusty plots in the middle of town.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，死者都被埋葬在小广场或教堂墓地里，埋在镇中心尘土飞扬的土地上。

sentences.en: Graves were all around.
sentences.zh: 墓地到处都是。

sentences.en: It was no big deal.
sentences.zh: 这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: Municipal burying grounds were right downtown, and they were relatively small, crowded places,
sentences.zh: 市政公墓就在市中心，而且是相对较小、拥挤的地方，

sentences.en: with really nothing much by way of landscape design.
sentences.zh: 在景观设计方面基本上没有什么讲究。

sentences.en: They were just, you know, the land surrounding a church.
sentences.zh: 它们只是，你知道的，教堂周围的土地。

sentences.en: This is Keith Egnor, professor of architectural history at the University of Oregon.
sentences.zh: 这是基斯·埃格诺尔，俄勒冈大学建筑史教授。

sentences.en: And in his book, Cemeteries, he talks about how these tiny, plain graveyards were hubs of activity.
sentences.zh: 在他的书《公墓》中，他谈到了这些微小而简陋的墓地如何曾经是活动的中心。

sentences.en: You might find a plumber or a bricklayer or a carpenter, you know, seated at a cemetery waiting for someone to come along and employ them.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现水管工、泥瓦匠或木匠，你知道的，坐在公墓里等待有人来雇佣他们。

sentences.en: Farmers would graze their cows in cemeteries because many people believed that the grass grown in churchyards or burial grounds was richer and made for sweeter milk.
sentences.zh: 农民会让奶牛在公墓里吃草，因为许多人认为教堂墓地或埋葬地生长的草更肥沃，产出的牛奶也更香甜。

sentences.en: Prostitutes even would sometimes be found in burial grounds.
sentences.zh: 甚至有时还能在墓地里发现妓女的身影。

sentences.en: So these were, you know, open public spaces in towns and cities, many of which didn't have much by way of alternative open public spaces.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是城镇中开放的公共空间，其中许多地方并没有太多可供选择的其他公共空间。

sentences.en: But by the 1820s and 30s, a couple things happened that changed how burials worked.
sentences.zh: 但到了19世纪20年代和30年代，发生了一些事情，改变了葬礼的运作方式。

sentences.en: Firstly, there's a series of outbreaks of disease, and cities were hit with waves of typhoid and cholera and yellow fever,
sentences.zh: 首先，爆发了一系列疾病，城市受到了斑疹伤寒、霍乱和黄热病的侵袭，

sentences.en: and it was just unsanitary to keep the deceased so close to the living.
sentences.zh: 把死者放在离生者这么近的地方实在是不卫生。

sentences.en: Also, cities were growing, and downtown real estate was becoming more valuable.
sentences.zh: 此外，城市在不断发展，市中心的房地产变得越来越有价值。

sentences.en: Gradually, in the United States, the lands of the living and the lands of the dead began to separate.
sentences.zh: 逐渐地，在美国，生者的土地和死者的土地开始分离。

sentences.en: Grave sites ended up far away from the city.
sentences.zh: 墓地最终搬到了远离城市的地方。

sentences.en: This model of a rural burial, separate from the city, took off in America in the 1830s,
sentences.zh: 这种远离城市的乡村墓地模式在19世纪30年代的美国兴起，

sentences.en: when Mount Auburn Cemetery opened outside of Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 当时马萨诸塞州剑桥市郊外的奥本山公墓开业了。

sentences.en: Well, Mount Auburn was what was called and what is still called a rural cemetery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，奥本山就是当时被称为、现在仍然被称为乡村墓地的东西。

sentences.en: What that meant was that it wasn't smack dab in the center of a town.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它不是坐落在城镇的正中央。

sentences.en: Also, it was one of the first cemeteries to actually be called a cemetery at all.
sentences.zh: 此外，它也是最早真正被称为公墓的墓地之一。

sentences.en: Previously, they'd been called, you know, burying grounds or burial grounds or churchyards.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，它们被称为，你知道的，埋葬地、墓地或教堂墓地。

sentences.en: Cemetery was a Greek word meaning sleeping chamber.
sentences.zh: 公墓（Cemetery）是一个希腊词，意思是寝室。

sentences.en: And just that word, cemetery, is so romantic and euphemistic.
sentences.zh: 仅仅这个词，公墓，就充满了浪漫色彩和委婉语气。

sentences.en: Death had once been deeply enmeshed in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 死亡曾与日常生活紧密交织。

sentences.en: Americans had home funerals in their front parlors
sentences.zh: 美国人在他们正面的会客室里举行家庭葬礼，

sentences.en: and encountered modest tombstones daily in their town squares.
sentences.zh: 每天在城镇广场上都能看到简朴的墓碑。

sentences.en: Mount Auburn made burial something removed from normal existence.
sentences.zh: 奥本山使葬礼成为一种脱离正常生活的事物。

sentences.en: Rural cemeteries were stately.
sentences.zh: 乡村墓地庄严宏伟。

sentences.en: They looked like they were a world apart.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像是一个与世隔绝的世界。

sentences.en: Mount Auburn was, and still is, beautiful, with emerald grassy hills and manicured hedges.
sentences.zh: 奥本山过去是，现在也依然非常美丽，拥有翠绿的草地山丘和修剪整齐的树篱。

sentences.en: There are statues of weeping angels and Egyptian obelisks, all connected with winding walking paths.
sentences.zh: 那里有哭泣天使的雕像和埃及方尖碑，全都由蜿蜒的小路连接在一起。

sentences.en: So it was a much more artful landscape modeled on the English garden tradition of picturesque landscapes,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个更具艺术感的景观，模仿了风景如画的英国花园传统，

sentences.en: as opposed to just simply a flat piece of ground with a bunch of stones, you know, lined up within it.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅是一块平地上排列着一堆石头。

sentences.en: This new style marked the beginning of the rural cemetery movement in America.
sentences.zh: 这种新风格标志着美国乡村墓地运动的开始。

sentences.en: And it would go on to influence the design of public spaces more broadly.
sentences.zh: 它后来对更广泛的公共空间设计产生了影响。

sentences.en: Because this was at a time when a lot of cities didn't have public parks or botanical gardens or museuMs.
sentences.zh: 因为当时很多城市还没有公共公园、植物园或博物馆。

sentences.en: These cemeteries then served as the model for some of our nation's first public parks,
sentences.zh: 这些公墓随后成为了我们国家最早的一些公共公园的蓝本，

sentences.en: such as Central Park in New York, which followed that picturesque garden approach that was first seen in our cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 例如纽约的中央公园，它就遵循了最初在我们的公墓中看到的风景如画的花园方法。

sentences.en: It was later picked up for college campuses, suburban subdivisions, and many other applications.
sentences.zh: 后来它被应用到大学校园、郊区住宅区以及许多其他领域。

sentences.en: The cemeteries in Colma were directly inspired by the Mount Auburn model as well.
sentences.zh: 科尔马的公墓也直接受到了奥本山模式的启发。

sentences.en: They were places to go to have picnics and amble around and get away from the smog and soot of neighboring San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 它们是人们去野餐、漫步、逃离邻近旧金山的烟雾和煤烟的地方。

sentences.en: If the city of the living was designed for speed and efficiency and business,
sentences.zh: 如果生者之城是为了速度、效率和商业而设计的，

sentences.en: the city of the dead was instead understood as a kind of quiet, peaceful Arcadia,
sentences.zh: 死者之城则被理解为一种安静、祥和的世外桃源，

sentences.en: a kind of evocation of paradise or heaven on earth where one would take one's eternal reward.
sentences.zh: 一种对人间天堂的唤起，人们在那里获得永恒的回报。

sentences.en: Oh, and about that eternity thing.
sentences.zh: 噢，关于那个永恒的事情。

sentences.en: That's very American.
sentences.zh: 这非常美国化。

sentences.en: Americans have a rather distinct practice of holding to burial in perpetuity.
sentences.zh: 美国人有一种相当独特的永久墓地保留习俗。

sentences.en: You don't find burial in perpetuity in that many other places.
sentences.zh: 你在其他很多地方找不到永久墓地。

sentences.en: By burial in perpetuity, he means a plot of land that is yours forever and ever until the end of time,
sentences.zh: 他所说的永久墓地，是指一块永远属于你、直到世界尽头的土地，

sentences.en: which is different than in, say, Argentina or France or Italy or any number of other countries around the world,
sentences.zh: 这与阿根廷、法国、意大利或世界上其他许多国家不同，

sentences.en: where families of the deceased typically lease a burial plot.
sentences.zh: 在这些国家，逝者的家属通常是租赁墓地。

sentences.en: It could be for five or ten years to a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 租期可能是五年、十年到一百年不等。

sentences.en: And if the family doesn't maintain that lease, then the remains are dug up or disinterred,
sentences.zh: 如果家属没有续租，那么遗骸就会被挖出或迁走，

sentences.en: and what is left is often burned.
sentences.zh: 剩下的东西通常会被火化。

sentences.en: The family is given the ashes and the plots are used for new burials.
sentences.zh: 骨灰交还给家属，墓地则用于新的埋葬。

sentences.en: And this almost never happens in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这在美国几乎从未发生过。

sentences.en: American cemeteries would rather double up on burials or do above-ground burials than dig up remains.
sentences.zh: 美国公墓宁愿重复埋葬或进行地上安葬，也不愿挖出遗骸。

sentences.en: That's just taboo.
sentences.zh: 这简直是个禁忌。

sentences.en: And that's why it was so strange in the early 20th century when almost all of San Francisco's dead were dug up and evicted to make room for the living.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在20世纪初，当旧金山几乎所有的死者都被挖出并驱逐以为生者腾出空间时，会显得如此诡异。

sentences.en: Which brings us back to the graveyards of Colma.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了科尔马的墓地。

sentences.en: What happened in 1900 was that the Board of Supervisors of the County of San Francisco decided that
sentences.zh: 1900年发生的事情是，旧金山县监事会决定，

sentences.en: they did not want any expansion of the cemeteries that were already in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望旧金山现有的公墓有任何扩张。

sentences.en: That's Maureen O'Connor again of the Colma Historical Society.
sentences.zh: 这是科尔马历史协会的莫琳·奥康纳再次发话。

sentences.en: So the legislation was that there would be no new burials in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 因此，立法规定旧金山不再允许新的埋葬。

sentences.en: And that went into effect in 1901.
sentences.zh: 该法案于1901年生效。

sentences.en: So no new burials.
sentences.zh: 所以不再有新的埋葬。

sentences.en: And that meant the existing cemeteries didn't have a reliable source of revenue.
sentences.zh: 这意味着现有的公墓没有了可靠的收入来源。

sentences.en: And so the cemeteries fell into disrepair and became these tiny wastelands for vagabonds and ne'er-do-wells and grave robbers.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些公墓年久失修，变成了流浪汉、无赖和盗墓贼的微型荒地。

sentences.en: And also they were gross.
sentences.zh: 而且它们还很恶心。

sentences.en: So in 1914, another ordinance kicked them out.
sentences.zh: 所以在1914年，另一项法令把它们赶走了。

sentences.en: They passed legislation that said not only no new burials, but these cemeteries just look awful.
sentences.zh: 他们通过立法规定，不仅不准进行新的埋葬，而且这些公墓看起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: They thought they were disease-ridden.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些地方滋生疾病。

sentences.en: So the city said the bodies have to be disinterred and moved.
sentences.zh: 因此市政府下令必须将遗体掘出并迁走。

sentences.en: From 1937 into the 1940s, most of the bodies from San Francisco were dug up and moved to Colma.
sentences.zh: 从1937年到20世纪40年代，旧金山的大部分遗体都被挖出并运到了科尔马。

sentences.en: Roughly 150,000 bodies in total.
sentences.zh: 总共大约有15万具遗体。

sentences.en: To move a body with the headstone cost the family $10.
sentences.zh: 连同墓碑一起迁移一具遗体花费家属10美元。

sentences.en: And if there was no money or no next of kin, the bodies were put into mass graves in Colma.
sentences.zh: 如果没有钱或没有近亲，遗体就会被安葬在科尔马的万人坑里。

sentences.en: But like, respectful ones.
sentences.zh: 但可以说是很体面的那种。

sentences.en: Because when you think of mass grave, you often think of mass executions.
sentences.zh: 因为当你想到万人坑时，你通常会想到集体处决。

sentences.en: And it was not that kind of process.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是那种过程。

sentences.en: It was a much gentler, respectful process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个温和得多、充满敬意的过程。

sentences.en: The deceased in the mass graves were blessed and memorialized and accounted for in records.
sentences.zh: 万人坑中的死者都受到了祝福、纪念，并在档案中有据可查。

sentences.en: And their headstones were reused as building material.
sentences.zh: 他们的墓碑被重新用作建筑材料。

sentences.en: Well, the mass grave headstones ended up along Ocean Beach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，万人坑的墓碑最终流落到了大洋海滩沿岸。

sentences.en: You'll see a lot of headstones out there.
sentences.zh: 你在那里会看到很多墓碑。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: They were used to keep from erosion.
sentences.zh: 它们被用来防止水土流失。

sentences.en: And if you find yourself in Buena Vista Park in the heart of San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己在旧金山市中心的美好远景公园，

sentences.en: look at the paved stones lining the trails and the street gutters.
sentences.zh: 看看小路两旁和街道排水沟铺设的石头。

sentences.en: And you'll see that a lot of them are cemetery headstones.
sentences.zh: 你会发现其中许多都是公墓的墓碑。

sentences.en: These headstones, sometimes faded fragments of them, sometimes completely intact,
sentences.zh: 这些墓碑，有时是褪色的碎片，有时完好无损，

sentences.en: are tucked all over the city, hiding in plain sight.
sentences.zh: 被藏在城市的各个角落，隐匿于众目睽睽之下。

sentences.en: And they are the closest contact most San Franciscans have with cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 它们是大多数旧金山人与公墓最近距离的接触。

sentences.en: There are only two graveyards left in the entire city.
sentences.zh: 整个城市里只剩下两座墓地了。

sentences.en: Death is a fact of life most urban dwellers don't see and don't think about.
sentences.zh: 死亡是大多数都市居民看不到也不去想的生活事实。

sentences.en: Whereas down in Colma, Maureen confronts her mortality every time she looks out her window.
sentences.zh: 而在科尔马，莫琳每次望向窗外时都会直面自己的必死命运。

sentences.en: I look out on the cemeteries and I think, you know, these people are resting in peace
sentences.zh: 我望着墓地心想，你知道的，这些人正在安息，

sentences.en: and sometimes I feel overwhelmed by all the things that I have to do.
sentences.zh: 有时我会被所有必须要做的事情压得喘不过气来。

sentences.en: But the day that I wake up that I don't have anything to do,
sentences.zh: 但如果有一天我醒来时发现自己无事可做，

sentences.en: I'm probably going to be moving into a cemetery.
sentences.zh: 我大概就要搬进公墓里去了。

sentences.en: Most people aren't sandwiched between two cemeteries
sentences.zh: 大多数人不会夹在两座墓地之间

sentences.en: and we don't really think about the question of what will happen to our bodies after we die.
sentences.zh: 我们其实也不会去想死后我们的身体会怎么样这个问题。

sentences.en: I ask the question and very often people are like a little taken aback.
sentences.zh: 当我问出这个问题时，人们往往会有点错愕。

sentences.en: Either they haven't thought about it or they, no, I haven't made any plans.
sentences.zh: 要么他们没想过，要么就是，没有，我还没做任何规划。

sentences.en: I certainly haven't made plans.
sentences.zh: 我当然也没做过规划。

sentences.en: And chances are you haven't either.
sentences.zh: 而且你大概也没做过。

sentences.en: I have no idea what will happen in my body after I die.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我死后我的身体会发生什么。

sentences.en: And that's kind of unusual in the course of history.
sentences.zh: 在历史的长河中，这其实挺罕见的。

sentences.en: It was indeed the case that, yes, people largely knew where they were buried.
sentences.zh: 过去确实是这样，是的，人们大都清楚自己会被埋在哪里。

sentences.en: Professor Keith Egnor says that prior to the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 基斯·埃格诺尔教授说，在南北战争之前，

sentences.en: Americans assumed they'd end up in their family plots or town churchyards
sentences.zh: 美国人认为他们最终会进家族墓地或城镇的教堂墓地，

sentences.en: and that their parents and children would be buried there too.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的父母和孩子也会埋在那里。

sentences.en: That is no longer the case.
sentences.zh: 现在情况可不这样了。

sentences.en: We move, you know, from job to job, from town to town.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们搬来搬去，换着工作，从一个城镇到另一个城镇。

sentences.en: We frequently encourage our children to, you know, go out and explore the world.
sentences.zh: 我们经常鼓励孩子们，你知道的，走出去探索世界。

sentences.en: And we, you know, we don't really know where we're going to be ending up.
sentences.zh: 而且我们，你知道的，其实并不知道我们最终会落脚何处。

sentences.en: Which is why today many people have opted not to be buried at all.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，如今许多人选择根本不进行土葬。

sentences.en: Cremation has become increasingly popular into our own time.
sentences.zh: 在当今时代，火葬变得越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: And this brought with it a number of new building types, crematoria,
sentences.zh: 这也带来了一些新型建筑，比如火葬场，

sentences.en: but also the public mausoleums where you have a small box containing an urn with ashes.
sentences.zh: 还有那种装着骨灰盒的小格子的公共陵墓。

sentences.en: But with cremation, you don't need a connection to one place.
sentences.zh: 但通过火葬，你就不再需要跟某个特定地方产生联系了。

sentences.en: Ashes don't have to stay displayed in a columbarium or a mausoleum.
sentences.zh: 骨灰不必一直陈列在骨灰龛堂或陵墓里。

sentences.en: They can be scattered anywhere you've ever lived or wanted to live.
sentences.zh: 它们可以被撒在你曾经住过或想住过的任何地方。

sentences.en: If your family and friends live all over the world, they can each have a part of you.
sentences.zh: 如果你的家人和朋友散落世界各地，他们每个人都可以拥有你的一部分。

sentences.en: And there are these services that you can order where ashes can be compressed into a diamond
sentences.zh: 而且现在有一些你可以订购的服务，能把骨灰压缩成钻石

sentences.en: and worn around someone's neck or turned into a hand-blown glass paperweight.
sentences.zh: 戴在某人的脖子上，或者做成人工吹制的玻璃纸镇。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of break, I think, ongoing over the course of the last hundred years or more
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在过去一百年甚至更长的时间里，正在发生某种程度的割裂，

sentences.en: in which people were perhaps much more rooted to the land, both in life and especially in death,
sentences.zh: 比起我们现在，过去的人们无论在生前还是尤其是死后，

sentences.en: by virtue of burial and knowing where they were going to be buried, than we are now.
sentences.zh: 凭借着土葬以及清楚自己将被埋在哪里，与这片土地有着更深厚的根基。

sentences.en: San Francisco's 19th century residents could never have guessed that they'd be evicted
sentences.zh: 旧金山19世纪的居民绝不会想到他们会被驱逐

sentences.en: and relocated miles away from their hometown to a city of the dead,
sentences.zh: 并被迁到距离家乡数英里外的死人城，

sentences.en: their headstone strewn about the parks and beaches of the city of the living.
sentences.zh: 他们的墓碑被随意散落在活人城的公园和海滩上。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffleman, with Lanny Hall, Emmett Fitzgerald,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由埃弗里·特拉夫曼制作，合作者包括兰尼·霍尔、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德

sentences.en: and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 还有我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Technical production and mix by Sharif Youssef, with music by Sean Rial.
sentences.zh: 技术制作与混音由谢里夫·优素福完成，音乐来自肖恩·里亚尔。

sentences.en: Katie Mingle is our senior editor, Kurt Kolstad is the digital director,
sentences.zh: 凯蒂·明格是我们的资深编辑，库尔特·科尔斯特德是数字总监，

sentences.en: and Taryn Mazza is moving to the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 泰琳·马扎即将搬到湾区。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Ashley Borman and Marcy Russell at the Chapel of the Chimes in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 本周要特别感谢奥克兰钟声礼拜堂的阿什利·博曼和玛西·拉塞尔。

sentences.en: This episode was inspired in part by our friends at KUOW in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的灵感部分来源于我们在西雅图KUOW的朋友们。

sentences.en: They have a new podcast called Terrestrial, where each episode explores
sentences.zh: 他们有一个名为《地球》的新播客，每期节目都通过

sentences.en: a personal question through the lens of climate change and the environment.
sentences.zh: 气候变化和环境的视角来探讨一个个人问题。

sentences.en: Ashley Ahern, the host of the show, has a whole episode about what we should do with our bodies
sentences.zh: 该节目的主持人阿什利·阿恩制作了一整期节目，探讨在环境不断变化的背景下，

sentences.en: when we die in light of our changing landscape.
sentences.zh: 我们死后应该如何处理自己的遗体。

sentences.en: And she features this architect, Katrina Spade.
sentences.zh: 节目中她采访了一位建筑师，卡特里娜·斯佩德。

sentences.en: My name is Katrina Spade, and I'm the founder and director of the Urban Death Project.
sentences.zh: 我叫卡特里娜·斯佩德，我是“城市死亡项目”的创始人和负责人。

sentences.en: Katrina's designed what she calls a recomposition center,
sentences.zh: 卡特里娜设计了她所称的“重组中心”，

sentences.en: a facility where it would be possible to compost multiple human bodies at a time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个能够同时将多具人类遗体进行堆肥的设施。

sentences.en: I realize this is pretty out there for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我意识到对很多人来说这有点太前卫了。

sentences.en: I know the Catholic side of my family would probably freak.
sentences.zh: 我知道我家族中信天主教的那部分人可能会抓狂。

sentences.en: But listen to the way she envisions one of these centers.
sentences.zh: 但听听她是如何构想其中一个这样的中心的。

sentences.en: And remember, it doesn't exist yet.
sentences.zh: 记住，这现在还不存在。

sentences.en: This is just how she imagines it.
sentences.zh: 这只是她的想象。

sentences.en: When you open the doors to the recomposition center,
sentences.zh: 当你打开重组中心的大门时，

sentences.en: the first thing you see is this three-story concrete form.
sentences.zh: 你首先看到的是这座三层楼高的混凝土结构。

sentences.en: It ends.
sentences.zh: 它到头了。

sentences.en: You can see the top of it.
sentences.zh: 你能看到它的顶部。

sentences.en: And wrapping around that core is a series of ramps that sort of meander.
sentences.zh: 环绕着核心的是一连串蜿蜒而上的坡道。

sentences.en: To hear the rest of the concept of the recomposition center
sentences.zh: 想要收听关于重组中心这一概念的其余部分

sentences.en: and some other ideas about the future of death,
sentences.zh: 以及关于死亡未来的其他一些想法，

sentences.en: check out the full episode when it comes out next Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 请关注下周二发布的完整节目。

sentences.en: That's May 16th.
sentences.zh: 也就是5月16日。

sentences.en: But for right now, you can just go subscribe.
sentences.zh: 但现在，你就可以去订阅了。

sentences.en: Again, that show is called Terrestrial.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，那个节目叫《地球》。

sentences.en: Check it out.
sentences.zh: 去听听看吧。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced on Radio Row
sentences.zh: 制作于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市

sentences.en: in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 风景秀丽的市中心电台街。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上找到该节目并参与有关节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me at Roman Mars and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上@我 Roman Mars，也可以@节目 99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and have a nice subreddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们在Instagram、Tumblr上都有账号，还有一个很好的Reddit子版块。

sentences.en: But we release at least two articles about design and architecture
sentences.zh: 但我们在官网上至少会发布两篇关于设计和建筑的文章，

sentences.en: that are just like the episodes,
sentences.zh: 内容就像节目一样，

sentences.en: but, you know, for reading on our website at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 不过呢，是供你在我们的网站 99pi.org 上阅读的。

sentences.zh: 电台乌托邦。
